title: fix: keep child completion responsive during database contention
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Gateway event handling stalling when a child run finishes while another process holds the shared state database.

## User Impact

Child completion and cancellation wait for their terminal signal without blocking unrelated Gateway work. Signal kinds, payloads, deduplication, retention, and best-effort recording behavior stay the same; no migration or operator action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The normalized terminal producer used the synchronous signal writer, so its SQLite coordinator wait ran on the event loop. It now uses the existing state worker, and each caller joins settlement with its current lifecycle or actor ownership. Transaction and commit admission reject superseded, corrected, or provisional outcomes before they can consume the first-write-wins terminal key.

The ACP test fixture now installs its in-memory flow store before constructing the task store, so the task store uses that same fixture owner. Terminal cases and the shared coordinator holder are extracted from oversized suites without weakening their assertions or deadlines.

## Evidence

- The real ACP manager contention regression passes with the worker producer and fails at the intended assertion against the original synchronous production code, using the same real SQLite coordinator holder and corrected fixture.
- 387 focused and sibling tests passed on Linux with Node 24 and pinned pnpm 12.4.2. After extraction, 299 affected tests and the relocated original-production negative were verified again. The final six registrar cases and unchanged real line-cap ratchet also passed. The isolated checks passed all 25 core-test type groups, core/root type checks, ratchets, formatting, docs/boundary guards, and dead-export scans. Lint stopped on the subsequently corrected error cause and three files byte-identical to the base; all required CI gates passed on the pre-refresh head `5c292289`.
- Real-worker tests cover transaction/commit owner revocation, corrected outcomes, newer runs, retired sessions, cancellation, and terminal deduplication. Managed reviews found no actionable P0–P2 defects, including the final structural extraction and subsequent cause-preservation correction.

The first CI run identified a missing error cause in the queued-cancellation guard. The correction preserves the caught cancellation error. The next run exposed three existing registry tests that checked final effects before worker settlement; those cases now join the existing root-work owner and keep their assertions/deadlines. The worker-access migration inventory now also marks child terminal outcomes as worker-backed. The full registry suite now passes all 188 tests.

A later CI failure came from session-sharing fixtures deleting their temporary databases before worker cleanup settled. The exact failing CI merge reproduced the retirement guard failure in its original 93-file, two-worker group; changing only the fixture lifecycle made all 1,175 tests pass. [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36159720429) and ClawSweeper review then passed on `5c292289`.

Main independently landed the same fixture ownership repair with an additional exited-maintenance-worker regression in #158205. Refresh `6d1e5c33` merges main `6d327782` and preserves that fixture byte-for-byte, removing it from this PR’s diff. Production blobs are unchanged, and the other clean overlaps preserve main’s changes. A fresh managed review found no actionable P0–P2 finding. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36164974540) and ClawSweeper review passed for the refresh, including `openclaw/ci-gate`.

<details>
<summary>Recorded time, memory, and test cost</summary>

The paired contention command used Linux, Node 24.19.0, and pnpm 12.4.2, with the same real coordinator holder and corrected ACP fixture. The holder releases independently after two seconds. The original synchronous producer prevents the next event-loop observation until completion settles; the worker producer yields while the lock remains held and joins completion after release.

| Paired command | Whole-command wall time | `time -v` maximum RSS |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Original production, expected negative | 33.75 s | 2,965,836 KiB |
| Worker producer, passing regression | 20.46 s | 3,156,628 KiB |

These command totals include worker-build/startup/transform work and were recorded before relocating the unchanged test body into its sibling file. Cache and startup costs were not normalized. Maximum RSS is the reported process high-water measure, not aggregate concurrent process-tree memory. These numbers describe proof cost; they do not establish a throughput, memory, or deployed latency improvement. The behavioral assertion establishes that the database lock wait no longer runs on the event loop.

After extraction, the five-file affected group passed 299 tests in 49.08 seconds for the complete command. Vitest reported these per-file test windows:

| File | Cases | Test-window wall time |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `session-state-events.test.ts` | 34 | 6.196 s |
| `manager.accepted-ownership.test.ts` | 9 | 1.775 s |
| `manager.terminal-signals.test.ts` | 2 | 3.255 s |
| `manager.test.ts` | 26 | 4.074 s |
| `subagent-registry-lifecycle.test.ts` | 228 | 11.917 s |

File windows exclude command setup/build and overlap in parallel execution, so they are not summed as CI cost. The new terminal-signal file contains the moved provenance case and the two-second contention regression; the lifecycle authority table adds five cases. These sampled test costs are not a whole-CI measurement. No marginal CI saving is claimed.

</details>

The isolated contention proof establishes removal of this blocking path. It does not establish a deployed latency improvement; representative post-deployment measurement remains outstanding.
